summary: The games roadmap distinguishes reusable producer/template qualification from each product’s installed and native acceptance. Templates composes the published reference; Game owns the shared WASM producer; SC2 and BAR retain product adapters, native gateways, clocks, receipts and authority, while FourD retains rules and saves. The selected presentation sequence is FourD before SC2/BAR; compatible WASM-only adoption can proceed without the FourD presentation pilot. Source delivery, image/build preparation and producer fixtures do not establish native gameplay, cleanup or product acceptance. FourD automated technical qualification also does not supply consenting-player evidence or permanent publication. Consult each owning plan for the exact accepted original and remaining boundary; this record creates no new dependency, operation grant or completion claim. The accepted FourD V2 amendment puts participant recruitment, paired comparisons and participant-derived selection outside automated technical acceptance. Remaining technical qualification, distribution and installed adoption proceed through their own capacity, custody and product gates without reopening the accepted technical submilestone. The original study and broader player outcome remain unfulfilled; automated tests establish neither comprehension, enjoyment, preference nor usability. Both candidates remain selectable without a supported winner; a later participant study requires consent and actual evidence.
title: Shared game producers and product acceptance have different owners
